articles.title: Asia’s Coal Prices To Stay High as Supply Drops and Demand Firms
articles.description: Thermal coal prices in Asia are expected to stay elevated in the coming months as demand is strengthening in the ongoing gas-to-coal switch, while supply from China and Indonesia is falling, Fitch Ratings said in a report. Coal prices in China, for example, have hit a three-year high in recent weeks as supply from key exporter Indonesia remains restricted due to government policies and strong El Niño disrupting river barge movements. Indonesia’s thermal coal exports have been crimped by government production quotas and heightened uncertainties…

articles.description: The wording has been a topic of intense discussions between the trade bloc and Norway, which has lobbied hard for the EU to abandon its climate-based opposition to oil and gas exploration in the high north.

articles.title: Copper Needs $332 Billion in New Mines to Avoid Deficit, BloombergNEF Says
articles.description: While nine out of ten key energy transition metals are back on track to deliver sufficient supply by 2050, a total of $332 billion of investment is needed in new copper mines to avoid a looming copper deficit that could slow electrification, BloombergNEF said in its Transition Metals Outlook 2026 on Tuesday. In recent years, supply of key energy transition metals has improved considerably, with the exception of copper, which is still expected to see a shortfall through 2050, unless billions of dollars are invested in new supply. articles.title: China Moves to Rein In Its Booming Hydrogen Industry
articles.description: China is eager to avoid overcapacity in yet another clean energy sector as it looks to curb excess hydrogen production amid overheated investments in projects. Over the past years, China, the world’s top solar equipment manufacturer, has grappled with overcapacity and price wars in the solar sector amid booming installations and solar equipment exports. articles.title: Oil-Rich Alberta Votes to Stay in Canada in Historic Referendum
articles.description: Albertans have rejected a proposal to move toward a separation from Canada, according to early results of the referendum held on Monday, as voters gave the federal government a boost to national unity. Residents of Canada’s oil province have voted to remain in Canada, CBC News projects based on the early results with still more than half of the votes to be counted. articles.title: Trump Announces $8 Billion in Emergency Diesel Relief for U.S. Farmers
articles.description: The U.S. Department of Agriculture will provide $8 billion in diesel fuel relief to American farmers for this year’s harvest season, to be distributed as one-time payments to eligible candidates. “This $8 billion investment will help bring certainty to our farmers during this harvest so they can continue to feed our nation,” Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins said in a news release. “President Trump is the most pro-farmer president of my lifetime, and he is continuing to put Farmers First every day,” Rollins remarked.…

articles.title: Asian LNG Prices Surge Past $30 as Middle East Shipping Risks Escalate
articles.description: Liquefied natural gas prices on the Asian spot market topped $30 per million British thermal units for the first time since December 2022, Bloomberg reported earlier today. The price jump follows a report about a strike on an LNG tanker in the Gulf of Aden, off the Yemeni coast. The UK Maritime Trade Operations outlet reported an LNG carrier coming under attack in the Red Sea, from a small boat, whose crew fired twice at the tanker. articles.title: Brent Tops $110 as Tanker Attacks Threaten Persian Gulf Supply
articles.description: Crude oil prices extended their climb today, with Brent topping $110 per barrel again earlier in the day, and WTI back at over $100, as traders turn increasingly pessimistic about the resumption of normal oil flows out of the Persian Gulf. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $109.68 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $98.55 per barrel. Brent crude is trading at its highest in five months. The price trend follows reports of intensive tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, which have severely affected oil flows, according…

articles.title: Robot Wars – How China Has the Robotics Industry in Its Grip
articles.description: Last year, China started requiring export licenses for rare earth magnets. Within weeks, Elon Musk was telling investors that production of Tesla's Optimus robot had been affected. That's because every humanoid robot needs up to 4.5 kilos of rare earth magnets to move, and China makes more than 90% of the world's supply. It's exactly the problem REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY) has been building to help solve. The company is putting together a rare earth supply chain outside of China, from processing in Saskatchewan to metal-making in Ohio.…

articles.title: UK Pays Record Sums to Balance Grid as Transmission Falls Behind
articles.description: The UK is among the most ambitious states when it comes to a transition to a net-zero economy. Also, the UK is struggling with some of the highest electricity prices in Europe—and is paying significant sums to maintain grid balance, even when its wind installations are generating plenty of electricity. Normally, the cost of maintaining a balanced grid, meaning stable and secure supply of electricity, is the highest when the weather affects alternative energy sources. articles.title: Why Invading Iran Could Become America's Biggest Military Mistake
articles.description: The ghosts of Baghdad and Kabul should be enough to silence any talk of sending American troops into Iran. Yet here we are, more than seven months into a war that began on 28 February with U.S.-Israeli strikes that killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, and voices in Washington and Tel Aviv are again whispering that only boots on the ground can finish the job. articles.description: The debate over new oil and gas fields usually ends in a familiar deadlock. articles.title: The Sulfur Crisis Threatening the World's Food Supply
articles.description: Sulfur has become an indispensable element for the modern industrial system, including agriculture. Before the outbreak of the Iran war, 24 percent of the world's supply of sulfur passed through the Strait of Hormuz. I can find no reliable information on whether sulfur is being shipped through the strait now after the Iranian government claimed control. I suspect the amount is close to zero. The sulfur price at the start of the Iran conflict was approximately $500 per metric ton for sulfur originating from the Middle East. It now sits above $800.…

articles.title: Qatar Offers Lebanon 2 Gas Plants and 20 Years of LNG Piped Through Syria
articles.description: Qatar is offering to take over Lebanon's power supply problem at no upfront cost to Beirut. A draft program seen by Reuters has Qatar building two gas-fired power plants within three years and QatarEnergy supplying the gas under a 20-year LNG contract, with private financing in place of Lebanese public money. The document leaves payment obligations and guarantees open for negotiation, and Lebanon's state utility currently delivers only a few hours of electricity a day. Pakistan’s economy grew by 2.0% in the quarter ended June, which is the fourth quarter of its fiscal year 2026, official data by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics showed on Monday.
